Input: height=32, width=32, years=1. All elevations are 1.

The program starts with boundary cells (row 0, row height-1, column 0, column width-1) in the queue. For a 32x32 grid, the boundary cells count = 32*32 - 30*30 = 1024 - 900 = 124.

All elevations are 1.

For year 1: pop all queue items with elevation <= 1. Initially 124 boundary cells with elevation 1. Popping each decrements remaining and adds unvisited neighbors.

The flooding spreads: all cells have elevation 1, so all cells get flooded at year 1. The BFS will eventually visit all 1024 cells. remaining starts at 1024, and each pop decrements by 1. So after processing, remaining = 1024 - 1024 = 0.

Wait, let me check: does the BFS reach all cells? Starting from boundary, elevation 1 <= year 1, so pop boundary cells, add their neighbors (visited). Those neighbors also have elevation 1 <= 1, so they get popped too (the while loop continues since queue[0][0] = 1 <= 1). This continues until all cells are popped. So remaining = 0.
